item.title: Severe storms likely in eastern Victoria on Sunday, Bureau says
item.description: The Bureau of Meteorology says a major thunderstorm outbreak is expected across eastern Australia on Sunday afternoon, with large hail and damaging winds possible in the north-east.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Severe thunderstorms are likely across a large part of eastern Australia on Sunday afternoon and evening, including eastern and north-east Victoria, according to the Bureau of Meteorology.

In its latest video update, current at midday on Saturday 24 October, the Bureau described "a major severe thunderstorm outbreak on Sunday afternoon, extending from eastern Victoria through western New South Wales and right up through western Queensland".

This story is based on that update. Forecasts and warnings change quickly – check the Bureau's latest warnings before you head out.

What the Bureau says for Victoria

  • Saturday night into Sunday morning: a cold front and trough are expected to bring rain to South Australia, Victoria and Tasmania, particularly late Saturday and into early Sunday – "plenty of rain during the night for Victoria and Tasmania", the Bureau said.
  • Saturday afternoon: the Bureau said severe thunderstorms were possible in parts of Victoria, with Melbourne's outer eastern suburbs the most likely part of the city to be affected.
  • Sunday afternoon and evening: the main outbreak. The Bureau said the Riverina, the area around Albury-Wodonga and north-east Victoria face the risk of "heavy rain, large hail and damaging winds", and that "destructive wind gusts are possible in perhaps one or two stronger supercell severe storms" in that area.

Across eastern Australia

The Bureau said many areas could get 20 to 50 mm of rain over about three days, mainly with thunderstorms, and well over 100 mm in some spots, particularly in central Queensland.

That follows a very wet week in Queensland, with flash flooding in the south-east. On Monday, the Bureau expects the storms to focus on north-east New South Wales and south-east Queensland, including Brisbane, Ipswich and the Gold Coast, in what it called the last day of this outbreak.

The Bureau said severe storms could bring down trees and power lines, and cause heavy rain, flash flooding and large hail. It said people had already been rescued after driving into flooded roads and creeks in Queensland.

What it means for you

  • Check the latest warnings and your local radar on the Bureau of Meteorology website or the BOM Weather app.
  • For warnings and incidents in Victoria, use VicEmergency.
  • VICSES says blocked drains, cars parked under trees and falling branches are some of the major causes of preventable storm damage.
  • For help with flood and storm emergencies, call VICSES on 132 500. In a life-threatening emergency, call Triple Zero (000).

Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, “Severe weather update: Major weekend severe storm outbreak”, video current 12 pm AEDT Saturday 24 October 2026; Bureau of Meteorology video news release, 23 October 2026; VICSES storm advice. item.title: Arden to get more than 5,400 homes and the City of Melbourne's first new public secondary school since 1910
item.description: Developers have been appointed for Arden Central next to the new Arden Station, and land has been secured for a new public secondary school.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
More than 5,400 homes will be built at Arden Central, next to the new Arden Station on the Metro Tunnel line.

The Victorian Government announced on 22 October that developers Hamton and Hostplus will deliver the precinct. The government says the number of homes is more than 50 per cent above the original target of 3,500, and more than 10,000 people will live there.

A new public secondary school

Land has been secured on two lots next to Arden Station, on Arden Street, for a new public secondary school.

It will be the first government secondary school built in the City of Melbourne since University High School was founded in 1910. The vertical school is meant to help meet growing inner-city enrolments. Land has also been identified for a future public primary school.

Deputy Premier and Minister for Education Gabrielle Williams said: "We are laying the groundwork for new schools where they are needed, including in Arden."

What's planned

Arden Central covers 12 hectares, 1.5 kilometres from the CBD. According to the release, it will include:

  • housing for first home buyers, families, key workers and students, with at least 10 per cent affordable housing
  • more than 4,000 homes designated for first home buyers, with Arden an anchor site for the government's First Home Buyers scheme
  • a 5,000-capacity live music venue run by Live Nation
  • a new Melbourne Victory campus, including a Women's Academy and youth female pathway program
  • shops, food and drink, and 5.5 hectares of open space.

When

Works are expected to begin in 2027, with around 1,700 homes completed by 2033.

The government says the project will support around 3,800 construction jobs and create more than 1,100 jobs across the precinct.

item.title: More than $36.8 million for flood levees, coastal defences and bushfire preparedness in Victoria
item.description: Eleven Victorian projects, including coastal protection at Elwood, will share more than $36.8 million in Round Four of the Disaster Ready Fund.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Eleven projects across Victoria will share more than $36.8 million to help communities prepare for floods, storms, rising seas and bushfires.

Federal Minister for Emergency Management Kristy McBain and Victorian Minister for Emergency Services Paul Edbrooke announced the funding on 22 October under Round Four of the federal government's $1 billion Disaster Ready Fund.

The Commonwealth is contributing more than $17.7 million, with a further $19.1 million from the Victorian Government and other project partners.

Elwood among the projects

A $7.2 million Coastal Risk Reduction and Resilience Program will deliver new and upgraded coastal protection at Elwood and Port Franklin. According to the release, it will reduce coastal flooding risks and improve resilience to storms and sea level rise.

Other projects named in the release include:

  • $12.3 million for levees along Racecourse Creek in Epsom, reducing flood risk to more than 500 homes and 60 businesses
  • $4.4 million for levee works at Castlemaine Caravan Park, Elizabeth Street and Campbells Creek Township
  • $3.7 million for a flood protection levee at the Rochester and Elmore District Health Service hospital, which was evacuated in the 2022 flood
  • nearly $3.9 million for community resilience and infrastructure projects in Mansfield Shire and Ruffy, to support residents before, during and after emergencies such as bushfires.

Victoria is also leading a $1 million project to share emergency information and deliver joint training between north-east Victoria and southern New South Wales.

The release says communities in Ruffy and Mansfield recently experienced fires, and communities in Bendigo and Rochester recently experienced flooding.

Mr Edbrooke said: "We know how quickly bushfires, floods and storms can turn lives upside down."

The full list of Victorian projects is on the National Emergency Management Agency's Disaster Ready Fund page.

item.title: Fibre broadband coming to more than 19,000 Victorian homes and businesses
item.description: A $133 million nbn co and Connecting Victoria program will bring fibre to the premises in 70 towns and suburbs.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
More than 19,000 homes and businesses in 70 Victorian towns and suburbs will be upgraded to fibre broadband, according to the Victorian Government.

Minister for Government Services Enver Erdogan announced the $133 million program on 22 October. It is a partnership between nbn co and Connecting Victoria.

What it means

The program will deliver fibre-to-the-premises technology, which runs high-speed fibre optic cable directly into each home or business. According to the release, this means download speeds of up to one gigabit per second.

The first upgrades are expected to finish in 2027, with the rest rolling out through to 2030.

More than 2,000 homes and businesses in Ararat, Donald, Castlemaine, Horsham, Mortlake, Sebastopol and Wendouree will be able to swap fixed wireless for fibre.

How it is funded

The upgrades are enabled by the expansion of nbn co's national fibre upgrade program, backed by a $3.8 billion Commonwealth funding package announced in January 2025, including $800 million from nbn co.

The government says Connecting Victoria has already improved internet for more than 100,000 homes and businesses in more than 180 towns and suburbs.

Check your address

To find out if you are eligible for current or future upgrades, use the 'check your address' tool on the nbn website, or register for updates at nbn.com.au/register.

item.title: New planning rules to protect Melbourne's green wedges and farmland
item.description: Statewide changes taking effect in November aim to limit the loss of rural land and reduce conflicts between new homes and established farms.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
New statewide planning rules aimed at protecting Melbourne's green wedges and Victoria's farmland from inappropriate development will come into effect in November, according to the Victorian Government.

Minister for Planning Sonya Kilkenny announced the changes on Thursday 22 October.

What the reforms do

According to the Victorian Government release, the reforms will:

  • strengthen green wedge and agricultural state planning policy
  • reduce the loss or fragmentation of rural land
  • support appropriate farm produce sales
  • minimise land use conflicts between sensitive developments, such as homes, and established farms
  • protect Victoria's food supply in planning decisions.

The release says statewide planning controls will also protect the urban growth boundary and support long-term planning for Victoria's growing population.

Why the change

The government says the changes respond to recommendations from the Green Wedge and Agricultural Land Action Plan 2024 and the Inquiry into Securing the Victorian Food Supply.

According to the release, that work found land use conflicts were making it harder and more expensive to grow food close to cities. The government says the new rules will give a consistent approach to protecting green wedges and farms from inappropriate development.

Minister for Agriculture Michaela Settle said the government was "protecting farms that are critical to the future of Victoria's agriculture sector".

item.title: $139.5 million for Victoria's integrity agencies as new anti-corruption laws begin
item.description: IBAC can now investigate a wider range of conduct and follow public money to private subcontractors on government projects.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Victoria's anti-corruption commission and two other integrity agencies will share $139.5 million in extra funding to start work under new laws passed by the Victorian Parliament in September.

The Victorian Government announced the funding on Thursday 22 October. It will support:

  • the Independent Broad-based Anti-Corruption Commission (IBAC)
  • the Victorian Ombudsman
  • Integrity Oversight Victoria.

The government says the money means the agencies can begin their work under the new laws immediately.

What the new laws change

According to the Victorian Government release:

  • The threshold of conduct IBAC can investigate has been lowered.
  • The definition of corrupt conduct now extends to serious disciplinary matters, including serious misconduct and conduct worthy of termination. There is a specific provision for elected officials: ministers, MPs and local councillors.
  • IBAC has new "follow-the-money" powers to trace public funds, so it can investigate private and third-party subcontractors on government projects.
  • The threshold for holding public hearings has been lowered by removing the "exceptional circumstances" provision.
  • There will be a legislated process for recruiting IBAC commissioners.
  • IBAC's budget requests and the Ministerial Code of Conduct will be published online.

In short

The changes widen what IBAC can look into, including the conduct of private and third-party subcontractors on government projects, and make it easier for the commission to hold public hearings.

Special Minister of State Ingrid Stitt said Victorians "rightly expect public money to be spent properly".

item.title: Planning starts on two new jobs precincts in Melbourne's west
item.description: Developers will fund planning and infrastructure for two new employment precincts in Melbourne's west, including one at Ravenhall, with public consultation to come.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Planning has begun for two new employment precincts in Melbourne's west. The Victorian Government release names them as the Ravenhall and Warrawee precincts, while its opening line places them in Ravenhall and Truganina.

Minister for Planning Sonya Kilkenny announced the start of planning works on Thursday 22 October. The government says the precincts will bring more jobs closer to where thousands of homes are being built.

A new approach

According to the release, the two precincts will pilot an industry-led approach, with developers working with the government on parts of the planning process.

The proponents, Boral, Dexus and Pelligra, will fund the planning and infrastructure improvements needed to unlock the land in the long term. The release says this includes major upgrades to arterial roads in the area.

Have your say

There will be public consultation so the community can have a say on the new developments. The release does not give dates.

Nearby growth

The release says more than 72 hectares of land in the same precinct was recently rezoned for industrial use through the Development Facilitation Program, creating more than 1,000 jobs.

It also points to Melton East, a new suburb the government says will deliver 12,000 homes, seven schools and more than five MCGs' worth of parks and reserves. Once complete, Melton East is expected to be home to more than 36,000 residents and support around 1,600 jobs.

item.title: Contract awarded to remove Anderson Street and Hudsons Road level crossings
item.description: Construction starts in 2027, with a new Spotswood Station due in 2028 and the project finished in 2029, the government says.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
A contract has been awarded to remove the level crossings at Anderson Street and Hudsons Road in Melbourne's west.

The Victorian Government announced on Thursday 22 October that an alliance of Acciona, WSP, Metro Trains Melbourne and VIDA Rail will deliver the project.

Why these crossings

The release describes Anderson Street as one of the most dangerous level crossings left on Melbourne's metropolitan rail network. It says there has been one fatality and four serious injuries there since 2006, and 26 near misses since 2016.

More than 6,000 pedestrians use the crossing each day, and the boom gates are down for half of the two-hour morning peak, according to the release.

At Hudsons Road, more than 6,600 vehicles use the crossing each day, with many waiting for long periods during the morning peak.

What's planned

Two new accessible underpasses will keep pedestrians and cyclists connected:

  • Anderson Street: stairs and two lifts on each side of the rail line, for cyclists and people with prams, mobility aids and wheelchairs
  • Murray and Goulburn streets: stairs and ramps.

The project will also create new open space on Anderson Street for outdoor dining, seating and public artwork. After community feedback, it will include more car parking to improve access to the Yarraville Village precinct, the release says.

Four rounds of community engagement have been held, and early designs for Anderson Street were released in May.

Timeline

According to the release:

  • Final designs: still to be released
  • Construction: starts in 2027
  • New Spotswood Station: opens in 2028
  • Project complete: 2029

Minister for Public Transport Vicki Ward said removing the crossings "will improve safety and cut congestion".

item.title: SEC Apprenticeship Academy pilot to take its first 40 electrical apprentices
item.description: Expressions of interest open in the coming weeks, with the first apprentices due to start early in 2027.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
The SEC Apprenticeship Academy is preparing to take its first electrical apprentices, with a 40-place pilot opening for expressions of interest in the coming weeks.

Minister for Energy and Resources Jaclyn Symes announced on Thursday 22 October that the SEC will partner with NECA Education & Careers and the Electrical Trades Union to launch the pilot.

According to the Victorian Government release, the first apprentices will start early in 2027. The release says the Academy will be Victoria's largest electrical apprenticeship training program, supporting 2,000 apprentices over four years.

Where the jobs are

The release says Victoria's energy workforce is expected to grow from around 45,000 workers today to 68,000 by 2040, with strong demand for electricians, plumbers and other skilled workers for network upgrades, home electrification and electric vehicle infrastructure.

Other projections in the release, all to 2040:

  • electricians in Victoria's energy sector to grow by more than 90 per cent from 2026, to around 8,500
  • almost 35,000 energy-sector workers across metropolitan Melbourne
  • jobs supporting home battery installations to almost triple, to around 2,600
  • jobs supporting electric vehicle infrastructure to quadruple, to around 14,300.

The release also says around 37 per cent of Victoria's energy jobs will be in regional Victoria. It does not say who produced these projections.

NECA Education & Careers CEO Gideon Perrott said the Academy would "give more Victorians the skills to turn that opportunity into a career".

How to find out more

Details are at secapprenticeshipacademy.necaeducation.com.au.

item.title: Volunteer Mark Edmonds named 2026 Victorian Senior of the Year
item.description: This year's awards also honoured work supporting people with dementia, older migrants, multicultural communities and female veterans.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Volunteer Mark Edmonds has received the Premier's Award for Victorian Senior of the Year 2026, recognising his work helping build self-sustaining communities in Zimbabwe.

Recipients were celebrated at Government House with Minister for Seniors Nick Staikos, the Victorian Government announced on Thursday 22 October.

Other award recipients

  • Sandra Verdam received the Positive Ageing Award for founding Memory Care Cafés, which support people living with dementia and their carers.
  • Ronnie Figdor OAM received the Promotion of Multiculturalism Award for his lifelong work building connections between diverse communities and generations.
  • Mahendrakumar Patel received the Emerging Impact Award for his work empowering older migrants and the multicultural community.
  • Margaret Jager received the Veteran Community Award for more than 40 years of service to Victoria's female veteran community.

Council on the Ageing (COTA) Victoria Senior Achiever Awards were also presented to nine Victorians. Their contributions range from mentoring and supporting vulnerable people to providing leadership and training during emergencies and disasters.

About the awards

For more than 30 years, the Victorian Senior of the Year Awards have recognised seniors who give back through volunteering, advocacy and community leadership.

Mr Staikos said this year's recipients showed "the extraordinary impact older Victorians have in our communities". He also encouraged people to get involved in Seniors Festival events running across the state.

Profiles of the 2026 recipients are at seniorsonline.vic.gov.au/awards.

item.title: Nearly 2,000 more registered teachers joined Victorian schools in a year, snapshot shows
item.description: The 2025 Victorian Teacher Workforce Snapshot projects 15,700 more teachers in the system by 2031.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Nearly 2,000 more registered school teachers joined Victorian schools between 2024 and 2025, according to the 2025 Victorian Teacher Workforce Snapshot.

Deputy Premier and Minister for Education Gabrielle Williams announced the figures on Thursday 22 October.

Key figures

According to the release:

  • More than 127,000 school and early childhood teachers are estimated to be ready to teach in Victoria's schools and kindergartens by 2031.
  • By 2031, Victoria is expected to have 15,700 more teachers in the system than in 2025.
  • Fully registered early childhood teachers rose 12 per cent in a year.
  • Victorian schools on average have fewer students per teacher than schools in all the other mainland states.
  • Victoria accounted for more than 84 per cent of the national increase in government school enrolments between 2018 and 2025.

Support for new teachers

The release says the Career Start program has supported more than 6,100 early career teachers since it began in 2021, and will support a further 2,500 in 2027.

More than 6,000 early childhood teaching scholarships have been awarded since 2019. The first fully funded Secondary Teaching Scholarships recipients will graduate and enter the workforce at the end of 2027, the release says.

According to the release, paid placements, employment-based degrees and targeted incentives are being used to get more teachers into regional and hard-to-staff schools and subjects. The government also says class sizes will be protected in the new enterprise bargaining agreement.

item.title: Preferred bidder named for Sunshine Station rebuild as Melbourne Airport Rail moves ahead
item.description: A CPB Contractors and SMEC alliance has been named preferred bidder to turn Sunshine Station into a six-platform hub, with a new Keilor East station linked to the Metro Tunnel due in 2031.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
A preferred bidder has been chosen to rebuild Sunshine Station in Melbourne's west as a major transport hub, as part of the Melbourne Airport Rail project.

The Victorian Government announced on Wednesday 21 October that the Network Integration Program Alliance, a partnership of CPB Contractors and SMEC, is the preferred bidder for the Sunshine Station works. The announcement was made by Victorian Premier Ben Carroll.

The Stage 1 works at Sunshine include two new platforms for regional trains, an extended station concourse, new forecourts on both sides of the station and an upgraded bus interchange. According to the release, the upgrades will turn Sunshine into a six-platform hub.

The project will also untangle six kilometres of track between West Footscray and Albion.

"Untangling the tracks will create capacity for 1,000 trains a day, including future airport services," Victorian Minister for Public Transport Vicki Ward said.

Stage 1 is due to be finished in 2030. The government says it will allow more frequent services on the Geelong, Ballarat and Bendigo lines and pave the way for future electrification of the Melton and Wyndham Vale lines.

Stage 1 is split into five works packages, and the release says three have already been awarded. Between them they cover moving underground utilities, reconfiguring tracks, building new rail bridges and building a new Tottenham Station. The fifth and final package, for a new Albion Station, is due to be awarded in 2027.

Stage 2 works are set to begin in the coming weeks and are due to be completed in 2031, when passenger trains will run to a new station at Keilor East. The release says the line will connect directly to the Metro Tunnel and have high-capacity signalling to allow frequent services.

The release does not give a cost for the works, a jobs figure or a date for when trains will first run to Melbourne Airport.

item.title: New MACHA app for Victoria's Maternal and Child Health nurses
item.description: A new digital platform will help MCH nurses share information and make referrals, with a statewide rollout from March 2027.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Victoria's Maternal and Child Health (MCH) nurses will get a new digital platform to share information and make referrals, with nurses getting access from December and a statewide rollout from March 2027, the Victorian Government says.

The Maternal and Child Health Application, or MACHA, was announced on Friday 23 October by Minister for Children Lizzie Blandthorn.

For Victorian families who see an MCH nurse in the early years of a child's life, the change is mostly behind the scenes – but the government says it should make care easier to coordinate.

What MACHA will do

According to the release, MACHA will:

  • help MCH nurses share information and make referrals with hospitals, councils and other support services
  • make it possible to access MCH and other support services in another part of Victoria for families who have temporarily moved
  • connect with the Parent Portal, which the government describes as a one-stop shop for trusted information, services and support for parents and carers.

“This platform will help nurses connect families with the services they need. Care will be more coordinated and more convenient,” Ms Blandthorn said.

Built with nurses

The government says MACHA was designed with MCH nurses, and that their decades of frontline experience sit at the heart of the platform.

When it starts

  • From December 2026: nurses get access through a dedicated training and transition environment, giving them time to learn the system and build confidence.
  • From March 2027: the statewide rollout begins.

MACHA is part of the government's children's digital reform program.

What it means for you

The release does not list any steps parents need to take. If you have questions about your child's MCH visits, your local MCH nurse or council MCH service is the place to ask.

item.title: Food relief grants: refrigerated van to stock The Big Umbrella's EAT.ATMs
item.description: The Victorian Government has announced $9.5 million in food relief grants for 177 organisations, including a refrigerated vehicle for a network of seven 24/7 meal machines.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
A Victorian charity that runs meal vending machines for people in need will buy a refrigerated vehicle with a Victorian Government food relief grant, as 177 organisations share in $9.5 million in funding.

The Victorian Government announced the 2026–27 Community Food Security Program grants on Friday 23 October. The announcement was made by Minister for Carers and Volunteers Luba Grigorovitch.

Meals on the move for The Big Umbrella

According to the release, The Big Umbrella will use its grant to buy a refrigerated vehicle to safely transport meals to its network of seven EAT.ATMs. The government says the machines provide discreet, convenient, 24/7 access to food for individuals and families in need, and are designed to reduce the barriers and stigma of asking for help.

The Big Umbrella said: “The EAT.ATM model is designed to remove barriers to food relief and make support available when and where people need it. This funding will help us expand our impact and ensure more individuals and families can access nutritious food with dignity and respect.”

Where the money goes

The release says the $9.5 million is split across two streams:

  • Local Grants: 168 organisations will share $7 million.
  • Coordination Fund: nine more organisations will share $2.5 million to strengthen food relief services across Victoria. They include The Community Grocer, SecondBite | FareShare, Alex Makes Meals and Foodbank Victoria.

Other funded projects named in the release include:

  • Common Ground Project on the Surf Coast, running food education and cooking programs for migrant and refugee women.
  • Asylum Seeker Resource Centre and Family Access Network, providing food relief to asylum seekers, young people and families facing hardship.
  • Enjoy Community Inc and Mullum Mullum Indigenous Gathering Place, expanding access to nutritious and culturally appropriate food.

The government says the funding will support food rescue, social supermarkets, meal production, affordable fresh food and better coordination between services, to help meet growing demand.

Find out more

The release does not list all 168 Local Grants recipients or the locations of the EAT.ATMs. You can read the full government media release.

Sources: Victorian Government media release, “Innovative Eat.ATMs Fight Food Insecurity Across Victoria”, 23 October 2026. item.title: Children’s Week starts this weekend with free events for families across Victoria
item.description: From cooking demonstrations in Dandenong to drumming in Geelong, 164 not-for-profit groups are running free activities from 24 October to 1 November.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Children’s Week runs from Saturday 24 October to Sunday 1 November, with free activities for children and families across Victoria.

Minister for Children Lizzie Blandthorn announced grants totalling $152,600, shared by 164 not-for-profit organisations to run Children’s Week events.

What’s on

Activities range from sport, cooking demonstrations and interactive drumming sessions to dance performances and traditional craft-making. The events are free and are hosted by not-for-profit groups, libraries and community groups.

This year’s grant recipients include:

  • Nourish Nation Foundation: cultural cooking demonstrations and activities in Dandenong
  • Bluebird Foundation: interactive drumming, songs and movement, led by One Spirit Africa, in Geelong
  • Malaysia-Singapore Sikh Association: Sikh and Punjabi festivities through dance, music, storytelling and cultural activities in Werribee
  • Thai Education Centre of Victoria: Thai culture through craft, traditional games, language, food, music and dance in Ballarat

This year’s theme

Last year, 29,500 children and families took part in 240 Children’s Week events supported by the Victorian Government.

item.title: Victorian dairy farms bounce back after tough season
item.description: A new report from the 20-year-old Dairy Farm Monitor Project shows 86 of 90 participating dairy farms made positive returns in 2025–26.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Victoria's dairy farmers have had a better year after a tough 2024–25 season, according to a new report.

The 2025–26 Victorian Dairy Farm Monitor Project Annual Report was released on 13 October by Agriculture Minister Michaela Settle. This year marks 20 years of the project.

What the report found

The project, run by Agriculture Victoria and Dairy Australia, tracks 90 dairy farms across northern Victoria, south west Victoria and Gippsland.

The report shows 86 of the 90 participating farms recorded positive returns. More than 80 per cent of participating farmers expect their returns to improve or stay stable in 2026–27.

According to the release, better conditions have helped farmers recover from drought, rebuild feed reserves and increase milk production. South west Victoria recorded the state's biggest improvement in dairy farm profitability.

Drought support

The government says that between September 2024 and September 2026:

  • more than 1,200 dairy farmers accessed drought grants of up to $5,000 statewide, or $10,000 in the south west
  • more than 480 dairy farmers received free expert advice to plan for and manage drought and reduce costs
  • it helped supply 48,000 tonnes of fodder and provided duty, fee and rates relief.

Twenty years of data

Dairy Australia chief executive Matt Shaffer said participation is growing, from 80 farms last year to 90 this year and an expected 110 next year.

Upper Murray farmer Evan Nicholas, who milks around 600 cows, has been part of the project for all 20 years. "Having 20 years of data gives us a really clear picture of how our farm has changed and where we've improved," he said.

Read the full report: 2025–26 Dairy Farm Monitor Project Annual Report (PDF), or see past reports on Agriculture Victoria's Dairy Farm Monitor Project page.

Sources: “Victorian Dairy Farmers Rebound in Milestone Year”, Victorian Government media release, 13 October 2026; Agriculture Victoria, Dairy Farm Monitor Project. item.title: Free legal help for Victorians building a home is expanding
item.description: The Domestic Building Legal Service will help homeowners at every stage of a build, not only after formal dispute resolution has failed.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Free legal help for Victorians building a home is being expanded to cover every stage of the build, through the Domestic Building Legal Service.

The Victorian Government announced on 22 October it would invest more than $14.5 million over five years in the service. Until now, it only stepped in after formal dispute resolution had failed.

What changes

According to the release, funding will rise from $730,000 to almost $3 million this year. The government expects:

  • up to 16,000 Victorians a year to use the service’s free online legal resources
  • around 1,100 homeowners to get tailored advice, online or in person
  • 400 homeowners a year to get intensive legal help, including advocacy and representation in complex disputes with their builder, up from 150 last year.

The service will be delivered by Justice Connect and the Consumer Action Law Centre.

The expansion was announced by the Minister for Consumer Affairs, Tim Richardson.

The background

The release says the collapse of builder Porter Davis in 2023 left 1,500 Victorian homes unfinished.

Since then, a new regulator, the Building and Plumbing Commission, has been set up. First-resort Home Warranty Insurance, covering lost deposits, unfinished work and defects, has applied since 1 July 2026, according to Consumer Affairs Victoria.

Explore: how a house gets built

Building a home in Victoria happens in stages: base, frame, lock-up, fixing and completion, with mandatory inspections by the building surveyor and progress payments along the way. Take a new home apart in 3D, stage by stage, and see what you can be asked to pay and what to check before you pay: How a house gets built, piece by piece.

The payment limits in the explainer are the current ones, according to Consumer Affairs Victoria: a deposit of up to 5% on contracts of $20,000 or more. Victoria’s new domestic building contract laws are set to start on 1 December 2026, according to Consumer Affairs Victoria, and the government has proposed new deposit and progress payment limits for homes, which it consulted on until 16 September. Anyone signing a contract from 1 December should check the rules that apply to them.

Where to get help

Help is available now from Justice Connect: justiceconnect.org.au/help/building-disputes.

General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Heat hits mums and babies hard, and the WHO wants countries to start counting the harm
item.description: The first-ever global indicators for tracking how extreme heat affects pregnancy, newborns and children have been launched, after babies under one faced 389% more heatwave days in 2024 than in 1986–2005.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Pregnant women, newborns and children are among the people most vulnerable to extreme heat, and the World Health Organization says health systems need to start measuring how it affects them.

On 21 October, the WHO, the World Meteorological Organization, UNICEF and the United Nations Population Fund launched the first-ever set of priority indicators to help countries track the health impacts of heat on pregnant women, newborns and children.

What the evidence shows

According to the WHO, exposure to extreme heat is linked to a 26% increase in the odds of preterm birth. Babies under one year old experienced 389% more heatwave days in 2024 than in the 1986 to 2005 baseline period, and an estimated 1.5 billion children worldwide are exposed to heatwaves that are becoming more frequent, longer or more severe.

“Heat is already affecting our most vulnerable populations, including pregnant women, newborns and children. But what health systems do not count, they cannot respond to,” said Dr Pascale Allotey, Director of the WHO’s Department of Sexual, Reproductive, Maternal, Child and Adolescent Health and Ageing.

What countries are being asked to track

The indicators ask countries to monitor preterm births, stillbirths, low birthweight, pregnancy hypertension, child deaths and health-facility visits during extreme heat. The WHO says monitoring school attendance can also help reveal how heat is disrupting children’s lives.

What the WHO wants

The WHO is urging all countries to develop and implement context-specific heat-health action plans that integrate the needs of pregnant women, newborns and children, strengthen early warning systems and trigger timely action when heat risks emerge.

Source: World Health Organization, New global framework launched to track increasing health risks of extreme heat for pregnant women, newborns and children, news release, 21 October 2026. Reported from the release only. Illustrations by The Dosage.

item.title: 100,000 more trees for Melbourne’s hotter suburbs
item.description: More than 100,000 trees will be planted in suburbs with less shade, and 10 shopping strips and streets will get a green makeover.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
More than 100,000 trees will be planted across Melbourne’s suburbs, with the focus on areas that have less tree cover and greater exposure to heat.

The Victorian Government announced the $3 million package on 22 October. It covers 23 projects across two programs.

Where the trees are going

The first program puts $1.5 million into 13 tree-planting projects. Planting will stretch from Werribee, Altona and Braybrook in the west, to Craigieburn, Sunbury and Broadmeadows in the north, and Pakenham, Cranbourne and Keysborough in the south-east.

The biggest projects include:

  • 16,000 trees across Hume
  • 14,000 trees at Cranwell Park in Braybrook
  • 15,000 trees along the Maribyrnong River and nearby reserves.

According to the government, the trees will provide more shade, cool neighbourhoods and create more habitat for native wildlife.

Greener shopping strips

The second program puts another $1.5 million into 10 projects to green busy shopping strips and streets.

These include shopping streets in St Albans, Sunshine West, Brunswick, Clarinda and Chelsea Heights, as well as streets in Richmond, Southbank and the CBD. The government says the extra greenery will cool these areas and make them more comfortable places to spend time.

Environment Minister Jaclyn Symes said the aim was to make everyday places “greener, cooler and better places to spend time”.

What comes next

The 100,000 trees are the first stage of a plan for 500,000 more trees and plants. The remaining 400,000 will be allocated in future rounds.

The government says this builds on 500,000 trees already planted across Melbourne’s west.

Source: Victorian Government, 100,000 More Trees To Help Melbourne Keep Its Cool, media release, 22 October 2026. Adapted from the release, © Copyright State Government of Victoria, used under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence; this version has been edited and shortened.

item.title: Why your protein shake clumps, and how Melbourne science could one day fix it
item.description: RMIT researchers have shown that static charge can be turned up, flipped or switched off with an electric field. Food powders are the next test.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Most people who drink protein shakes have chipped a stubborn lump out of the bottom of a shaker, or chased a floating clump around a mug of chocolate milk. According to researchers at RMIT University, static electricity is one of the likely reasons, and they have found a way to control it.

Scientists from RMIT and Riga Technical University in Latvia have shown that the static charge left on a surface can be controlled. RMIT says the discovery could help manufacturers avoid unwanted static when making everyday household goods, and might one day stop powders such as protein, chocolate malt and coffee from clumping.

A costly little zap

Static electricity is usually treated as a hazard. Industry often reduces it by adding expensive conductive additives, a one-size-fits-all fix. According to RMIT, static discharge costs the electronics industry alone about US$5 billion.

The new findings point to a different approach: surfaces whose static charge could be programmed to suit the job.

What the researchers found

The study was co-led by Dr Peter Sherrell from RMIT’s School of Science, in collaboration with Riga Technical University. It showed that applying an electric field while two surfaces touch and pull apart controls how much static charge is left behind. The field can also decide whether that charge is positive or negative, or remove it altogether.

The first author and co-corresponding author is Dr Andris Šutka of Riga Technical University. Professor Amanda Ellis from the University of Melbourne is a co-author, and PhD student Dumindu Dassanayaka and Dr Qiang Sun from RMIT were also key contributors.

Dr Sherrell gave the example of a conveyor belt sorting seeds, where the static charge changes with the size or species of seed. Adjusting the electric field for each species would mean “no risk of a seed getting a static shock”, he said.

Other possible uses include anti-static surfaces for manufacturing and electronics, controlling where charged particles or plastics stick and how they assemble, smarter sensors, and smart air and gas filters.

A smoother shake?

As powders rub and tumble during manufacturing, packing and pouring, the grains can pick up static charge and cling to each other.

“In principle, we could apply a small electric field across powders as they move,” Dr Sherrell said. That would stop the grains charging up, so they don’t get electrostatically “stuck” to each other.

The team tested plastics, not food. RMIT says the results are a good indicator of how the approach could work for food powders, and the next step is to find out how strong the field needs to be, how long to apply it for each powder, and where in the process it works best.

The researchers also plan to test real powders and to study programmable surfaces at much smaller scales, so different parts of one surface could be programmed differently. A current grant application with industry partners focuses on removing anti-static additives from fuels by tuning the surfaces the fuels touch, which could make fuel more energy efficient.

Solving a long-standing puzzle

The research also adds evidence to a question scientists have debated for years: what makes electric charge separate when two materials touch and pull apart?

Computer simulations showed that the fields the team applied were similar in strength to those created naturally when rough plastic surfaces press together. According to RMIT, this supports the idea that tiny built-in electric fields help drive everyday static electricity.

How the research was done

The team pressed polystyrene films together and pulled them apart 500 times while applying external electric fields. Stronger fields left more charge, and reversing the field from positive to negative reversed the charge. The same thing happened in every plastic tested. The results were then compared with computer models to understand what was happening.

The limits

The experiments were done in a lab on plastic films, mostly polystyrene. Protein, malt drink and coffee powders were not tested. The charge was set by applying a field during contact and measured afterwards, so switching the charge live, as in the conveyor belt example, has not yet been shown. The simulations used a simplified model, and the approach has not been tried on industrial equipment.

“The science would enable this to happen based on the discovery,” Dr Sherrell said.

Why it matters to you

For now, your shaker still needs a good shake. But if the approach works on real powders, the lumps in protein, malt and coffee could one day be a thing of the past.

The study, “Electric fields control static charge during contact-friction-separation”, is published in Nature Communications. It was supported by the Latvian Central Finance and Contracting Agency (ERC project TriboCharge) and an RMIT Vice-Chancellor’s Research Fellowship.

Sources: RMIT University, media release, 21 October 2026; Šutka, Sherrell et al., “Electric fields control static charge during contact-friction-separation”, Nature Communications, 15 October 2026 (DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-77733-4).

item.title: Sri Lanka chase down 430 to stun England in Rawalpindi
item.description: A record-breaking night in Pakistan, new umpires in Colombo and a WBBL season starting without Chamari.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage Sport Desk
item.content:encoded:
Sri Lanka Cricket: The Week · 17–23 October 2026

Sri Lanka’s men produced one of the great one-day run chases on Thursday, hunting down England’s 429 for 4 in Rawalpindi with a ball to spare. It was the second-highest successful chase in men’s ODI history and came only four days after a 37-run loss to Pakistan in the tri-series opener. With two group games left in Lahore, the side is right in the race for the 31 October final.

430Sri Lanka’s winning target against England
97Dasun Shanaka, from 50 balls
130Pavan Rathnayake’s century
51new Level 5 umpires certified by SLC

Sri Lanka men’s internationals

Record chase sinks England. England batted first and posted 429 for 4, the highest total Sri Lanka have ever conceded in an ODI. Harry Brook made 202, England’s first ODI double century (ESPNcricinfo; Prothom Alo). Sri Lanka slipped to 24 for 2 in the fifth over, then Pavan Rathnayake (130 from 106 balls) and Avishka Fernando (97 from 83) added 166 for the third wicket. Dasun Shanaka, promoted up the order, smashed 97 from 50 balls with eight sixes, and Janith Liyanage (61 not out from 27) finished it with a six off the second-last ball. Sri Lanka reached 430 for 8 in 49.5 overs to win by two wickets (scorecard, CREX; Rajasthan Royals match report). Reports say only South Africa’s 2006 chase against Australia in Johannesburg has been bigger.

Opening loss to Pakistan. In the first tri-series match on 18 October, Sri Lanka won the toss and bowled, dismissing Pakistan for 305 in 49.5 overs. Eshan Malinga took four wickets and Asitha Fernando three. Captain Salman Ali Agha’s century (107) proved the difference, as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 268 and lost by 37 runs (Radio Pakistan; Ada Derana).

The road to the final. Pakistan top the table with two wins from two, Sri Lanka have one win and England none (ESPNcricinfo). Beating England in Lahore on 29 October would guarantee Sri Lanka a place in the 31 October final, barring washouts.

Nissanka watch. Opener Pathum Nissanka misses the tri-series with a hamstring injury, and Lahiru Udara has come into the ODI squad (Express Tribune). Nissanka is named in the 15-man Test squad under new Test captain Kusal Mendis, but will travel only if he is declared medically fit (SLC media release, Test squad). The first Test starts in Rawalpindi on 9 November.

Women’s cricket

Quiet week. Sri Lanka women had no matches or squad news this week. Looking ahead, Australia’s women arrive on 10 December for three ODIs at Dambulla on 15, 18 and 20 December, part of the ICC Women’s Championship (SLC media release, Australia women’s tour).

Domestic and LPL

51 new umpires certified. Sri Lanka Cricket presented certificates to 51 umpires (47 men and four women) who passed the Level 5 exam, the entry point for umpiring in Sri Lanka. They can now stand in SLC’s District and Provincial tournaments and begin a pathway through Levels 4, 3 and 2 towards First Class status. Former ICC umpires Asoka De Silva and Lyndon Hannibal, now SLC’s Senior Manager, Umpire Development, attended the ceremony at SLC headquarters (SLC media release, Level 5 umpires).

Major Club four-day fixtures out. SLC has published the 2026/27 fixtures for the Major Club 4 Day League, the country’s top domestic first-class competition (SLC media release, fixtures). The full draw is on the SLC site.

LPL. No new Lanka Premier League announcements this week.

Sri Lankan players in Australia

Chamari not back at the Thunder. Sydney Thunder have chosen not to take up the third-year option on Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu’s contract, using the list spot to keep Tahlia Wilson. Athapaththu does not appear on any club’s list for the new season (cricket.com.au; Sportstralia). The league has dropped its overseas draft and gone back to direct signings, so a late deal with another club is still possible.

WBBL starts in Melbourne. WBBL|12 opens on Thursday 29 October with a double-header at Junction Oval: Renegades v Thunder in the afternoon, then Stars v Hurricanes at 7.10pm under the ground’s new lights (cricket.com.au). A good chance for local fans to get to a game. Read our WBBL preview →

Coming up

  • Tue 27 Oct: Pakistan v Sri Lanka, tri-series, Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore. 1.30pm PKT / 7.30pm AEDT
  • Thu 29 Oct: England v Sri Lanka, tri-series, Lahore. 7.30pm AEDT
  • Thu 29 Oct: WBBL|12 opens, Junction Oval, St Kilda. Stars v Hurricanes 7.10pm AEDT
  • Fri 30 Oct – Sun 1 Nov: Hong Kong Sixes, Kowloon. Sri Lanka (captain Sangeeth Cooray) are in Group B with Bangladesh and Scotland. Times to be confirmed (SLC media release, squad)
  • Sat 31 Oct: Tri-series final, Lahore (top two teams). 7.30pm AEDT
  • Further ahead: three-day tour match in Islamabad, 4–6 November; first Test v Pakistan, Rawalpindi, from 9 November

Sources: ESPNcricinfo, CREX scorecard, Sri Lanka Cricket media releases (srilankacricket.lk), Prothom Alo, Rajasthan Royals, Radio Pakistan, Ada Derana, Express Tribune, WION, The Papare, Wisden, cricket.com.au, Sportstralia. All times Melbourne (AEDT).

item.title: Megan Schutt suspended for two matches
item.description: Cricket Australia says a single, out-of-competition breach of its prescription-medication rules was not performance-enhancing.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Australian cricketer Megan Schutt has been suspended for two matches, Cricket Australia announced on 22 October.

According to Cricket Australia, Schutt failed to follow its Sports Science and Sports Medicine guidelines on prescription medication.

The governing body said the breach was a single incident that happened out of competition, and was “not for performance enhancing purposes”.

The two-match ban covers all international and domestic cricket.

In its statement, Cricket Australia said it would keep supporting Schutt and reinforce “the standards and responsibilities expected of everyone representing our game”.

item.title: Smart glasses to be banned in every Victorian school from 2027
item.description: From term 1, phones, smart glasses and other personal devices must be switched off and stored. Here’s what it means for students, parents and volunteers.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Smart glasses will join phones on the list of devices banned during the school day at every Victorian school from the start of 2027, under new rules announced on Wednesday.

What changes for students

From term 1, 2027, students at government, Catholic and independent schools must keep phones, smart glasses and other personal electronic devices switched off and stored during school hours and school activities.

What changes for adults

In government schools, teachers, parents and volunteers will not be allowed to wear smart glasses or other covert filming devices on school grounds, or on school-organised activities such as camps and excursions. This applies at all times, not just during school hours, and to government school students as well.

The one exception

Smart glasses are allowed only as a reasonable adjustment for a person with disability, when no other suitable adjustment can be provided.

Why it matters to you

If your child has smart glasses, they will need to be switched off and stored during school hours and school activities from term 1, 2027.

If you are a parent or volunteer at a government school, you won’t be able to wear smart glasses on school grounds, camps or excursions at any time.

Source: Victorian Government, Smart Glasses To Be Banned In All Victorian Schools, media release, 21 October 2026. Adapted from the release, © Copyright State Government of Victoria, used under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence; this version has been edited and shortened.

item.title: Going home to Sri Lanka? What to know about dengue and the new vaccine
item.description: Sri Lanka has passed 100,000 dengue cases this year. For the first time, people in Australia can be vaccinated before they fly. Here’s who it’s for, and how to plan around it.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Every trip home comes with a list: gifts for the cousins, the aunties to visit, the long drive from Katunayake. This year there is one more thing worth adding, and it needs to be done months before the suitcase comes out.

Sri Lanka has passed 100,000 dengue cases this year. And since this month, Australians have a dengue vaccine they can get from their own GP.

100,871dengue cases in Sri Lanka this year, as reported on 4 October
78deaths
52,906cases in Western Province, which includes Colombo and Gampaha

Gampaha alone has recorded 21,377 cases, the most of any district, according to figures from the National Dengue Control Unit.

WHAT THE OFFICIAL ADVICE SAYS

  • Registered by the Therapeutic Goods Administration in April 2026 for ages 4 and over.
  • Two doses, at least 12 weeks apart. Both matter.
  • On private prescription. Not free under the National Immunisation Program.
  • No blood test needed to check if you’ve had dengue before. Your doctor goes by your history.
  • Had dengue recently? Doctors may wait six months after the illness.
  • Allergic reactions are rare: about 29 per million doses in overseas monitoring. You’ll be asked to wait 15 minutes after the injection.
  • No booster is recommended yet.
  • Can be given with other travel vaccines, such as hepatitis A, typhoid or yellow fever.
Sources: ATAGI statement, 24 Sept 2026; Takeda Australia, 1 Oct 2026.

The vaccine

The vaccine is called Qdenga. The Therapeutic Goods Administration registered it in April for people aged four and over, and its maker, Takeda, announced on 1 October that it is now available in Australia. It is on private prescription, through your GP or a travel clinic, and it is not on the National Immunisation Program, so you will pay for it. Ask what it costs when you book.

Who should get it

Australia’s immunisation advisers, ATAGI, set out who it’s for in a statement published on 24 September.

A “likely history” means something like a dengue-type illness during a trip or within two weeks of coming home. ATAGI says a blood test to check for past dengue isn’t routinely recommended. People living with HIV who are not immunocompromised can have it. Takeda adds that safety and effectiveness haven’t been established in people over 60. The trial that measured protection was done in children; there are no efficacy figures for adults, but ATAGI says adults’ immune response to the vaccine is similar.

Timing matters

Because the doses are at least 12 weeks apart, it is already too late to fit both in before Christmas. For the Sinhala and Tamil New Year in April, the first dose needs to be in by mid-January. If you can only fit in one dose before you fly, ATAGI says to have it anyway: in the trial, in children, one dose was 82% effective against lab-confirmed dengue in the three months before the second. That is not a guarantee for adults, and both doses are still needed for the fullest protection. Make a plan for the second dose, either when you’re back or with a vaccination provider in Sri Lanka, if one can give it, when it’s due.

The vaccine isn’t the whole answer

The mosquitoes that carry dengue, Aedes aegypti, bite mainly during the day, not just at dusk. The World Health Organization advises:

  • repellent with DEET, picaridin or IR3535
  • clothing that covers as much of your body as possible
  • screens or nets, including for daytime naps
  • emptying anything that holds water around the house you’re staying in, once a week

Smartraveller says the risk of mosquito-borne illness is higher in the wetter months: May to October in the south-west, including Colombo, and December to March in the north-east.

If you get sick

Symptoms usually start four to 10 days after the bite: a high fever, a bad headache, pain behind the eyes, aching muscles and joints, and sometimes a rash. The WHO advises paracetamol for fever and pain, not ibuprofen or aspirin, which can make bleeding more likely.

Get help straight away if the fever drops but you feel worse: severe stomach pain, vomiting that won’t stop, bleeding gums or nose, or fast breathing. Back in Australia, tell your doctor where you’ve been.

The Conversation has also reported on the vaccine for travellers. Sources: ATAGI statement on the clinical use of the dengue vaccine Qdenga for Australians, 24 September 2026; Takeda Australia, QDENGA now available in Australia, 1 October 2026; National Dengue Control Unit figures, reported by The Morning, 4 October 2026; WHO dengue fact sheet; Smartraveller: Sri Lanka. This is general information, not medical advice: talk to your GP.

item.title: A bigger emergency department opens at the Royal Children’s in December
item.description: Twenty more treatment spaces and more than 85 extra staff should let the hospital see about 13,000 more children a year. Here’s what changes, and where else to go when it isn’t an emergency.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Every parent in Melbourne knows the waiting room at the Royal Children’s Hospital in Parkville. It already sees more than 80,000 emergency patients a year. From December, it gets bigger.

The expanded emergency department opens this December, the Victorian Government announced on 16 October, with $66 million to staff the new spaces from the first day. The hospital says the bigger department will have about a third more treatment spaces and a second waiting room.

13,000more children a year expected to be treated
20extra treatment spaces

What’s new

  • 20 extra treatment spaces, including new cubicles, short-stay beds and fast-track bays.
  • A second waiting room, according to the hospital.
  • A new procedure room, so minor procedures can be done in the emergency department without admitting a child to a ward.
  • More than 85 extra full-time positions, including up to 25 graduate nurses.

It is the second stage of the hospital’s expansion. The first stage, a new 30-bed ward, is already open and treating about 2,730 more children a year, the government says.

When it isn’t an emergency

A bigger emergency department helps, but for many fevers, sprains and earaches there are faster free options in Victoria:

  • NURSE-ON-CALL on 1300 60 60 24, 24 hours a day, for advice from a registered nurse.
  • Victorian Virtual Emergency Department at vved.org.au: a free video call with an emergency doctor or nurse, 24 hours a day.
  • Medicare Urgent Care Clinics: walk-in, bulk-billed care for urgent but not life-threatening problems, usually open from 8am to 10pm. Find one at Better Health Channel.

If your child has trouble breathing, is unconscious or you think their life is at risk, call Triple Zero (000).

Sources: Victorian Government, Royal Children’s To Treat An Extra 13,000 Kids A Year, 16 October 2026; The Royal Children’s Hospital, Expansion Project; Better Health Channel. General information, not medical advice.

item.title: Melbourne Fashion Week takes over City Square this Saturday, and it’s free to stand and watch
item.description: Two outdoor runways on Saturday 24 October, a ticketed closing show on Sunday, and more than 100 events across the city this week.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
For one week, the City of Melbourne wants the whole city to feel like a catwalk. Melbourne Fashion Week runs until Sunday 25 October, with runway shows, exhibitions, workshops and talks, and the City of Melbourne says there are more than 100 events in the program.

The easiest way in costs nothing. On Saturday, City Square, on the corner of Swanston and Collins streets, becomes an outdoor runway.

Sat 24two free outdoor runways in City Square

item.title: Three steps that could save a life this Shocktober
item.description: Around 21 Victorians have a cardiac arrest every day and only one in 10 survives. Ambulance Victoria’s free guides show you what to do, including in Tamil.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
October is Shocktober, Ambulance Victoria’s month-long push to get more people to learn CPR and how to use a defibrillator (AED). The reason is simple: when someone’s heart stops, what bystanders do in the first few minutes decides whether they live.

21Victorians have a cardiac arrest every day
1 in 10survive

For every minute CPR is delayed, the chance of survival drops by 10 per cent, Ambulance Victoria says. If the person gets CPR and a shock from a defibrillator before paramedics arrive, their chance of survival more than doubles.

Call, Push, Shock

If someone collapses and isn’t breathing normally:

  1. Call Triple Zero (000). The call taker will talk you through CPR and using a defibrillator.
  2. Push on the centre of the chest, between the nipples. Push hard, to a steady rhythm.
  3. Shock: if there’s a defibrillator nearby, turn it on and follow its instructions.

You can find the nearest registered defibrillator on Ambulance Victoria’s AED map. If you know CPR, the free GoodSAM app can alert you when someone nearby has a cardiac arrest. Ambulance Victoria is running free CPR and AED sessions across the state this month; see its Shocktober events page.

Guides in your language

Ambulance Victoria publishes its Call Push Shock guide and videos in 16 languages besides English, including Tamil, Malay and Vietnamese.

For Tamil-speaking families, the Tamil leaflet and video are worth sharing with parents and grandparents.

Why it matters to you

A cardiac arrest can happen anywhere, including at home in front of family. Learning these three steps takes a few minutes. If you have older relatives living with you, make sure everyone in the house knows them.

Sources: Ambulance Victoria, Shocktober and Call Push Shock, accessed 15 October 2026; Multicultural and Multifaith Victoria e-news, 15 October 2026. General information, not medical advice. In an emergency, call 000.

item.title: Australia is Sri Lanka’s fourth-biggest source of visitors so far this October
item.description: New official figures show 77,868 tourists arrived in the first half of the month. India is far ahead, and Australia sits in fourth place.
item.dc:creator: The Dosage
item.content:encoded:
Sri Lanka welcomed 77,868 international tourists between 1 and 15 October 2026, according to the latest weekly arrivals report from the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA).

India was again by far the largest market, with 29,323 visitors, almost 38 per cent of the total. China (5,988) and the United Kingdom (5,291) came next. Australia was fourth with 4,187 arrivals, roughly one in every 19 visitors. Germany, Russia, France, Pakistan, the United States and the Maldives rounded out the top 10.

Since 1 January, 1,771,547 tourists have arrived in Sri Lanka. Australia is fifth for the year with 91,176 visitors, behind India, the UK, China and Germany.

77,868arrivals, 1–15 October
4,187from Australia, fourth after India, China and the UK
1,771,547arrivals in 2026, to 15 October
2,362,521arrivals in 2025, the record year

What the numbers tell us

These points are The Dosage’s own calculations from the SLTDA figures:

  • Sri Lanka averaged about 5,190 arrivals a day in the first half of October.
  • If that pace held for the whole month, October would finish at around 161,000 visitors. That is a little below the 165,193 recorded in October 2025. SLTDA has not published a same-period comparison, so treat this as a rough guide only.
  • The 2025 full-year total was 2,362,521. To match it, Sri Lanka needs about 591,000 more arrivals between 16 October and 31 December. That works out to about 7,675 a day, well above the current pace.

Why it matters to you

  • If you have family in tourism: Hotels, guesthouses, drivers, guides and restaurants rely on these numbers. A steady flow from Australia is good news for businesses that host Australian travellers.
  • If you are planning a trip home: The report counts arrivals only. It says nothing about fares or room rates, so compare prices early if you are travelling for the December and January holidays.
  • If you follow Sri Lanka’s economy: Visitor numbers are one of the quickest monthly signals of how the recovery is tracking. Watch for SLTDA’s full October figures.

Sources: Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority, Weekly Report 1st to 15th October 2026; SLTDA Weekly Tourist Arrivals Reports 2026.
